topic.name: Combining Graph Transformations of Reciprocal Functions

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y = \dfrac{4}{x}?$
question.explanation:
To plot $y = \dfrac{4}{x},$ we apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y=\dfrac{1}{x}.$
  • Stretch the result by a scale factor of $4$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=\dfrac{4}{x}.$

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y = \dfrac{1}{2(x+1)}?$
question.explanation:
To plot $y = \dfrac{1}{2(x+1)},$ we apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y=\dfrac{1}{x}.$
  • Translate it by $1$ unit to the left to get the graph of $y=\dfrac{1}{x+1}.$
  • Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $\dfrac 1 2$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=\dfrac{1}{2(x+1)}.$

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y = \dfrac{4}{5x}+3?$
question.explanation:
To plot $y = \dfrac{4}{5x}+1,$ we apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y=\dfrac{1}{x}.$
  • Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $\dfrac 45$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=\dfrac{4}{5x}.$
  • Translate it by $3$ units up to get the graph of $y=\dfrac{4}{5x}+3.$

exampleAnswers.title: Solving for Some Unknowns Given the Graph of a Transformed Reciprocal Function

question.text: The graph represents the function $y = \dfrac{a}{x-b}+k.$ What are the values of $a,$ $b,$ and $k?$
question.explanation:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=1.5,$ while the vertical asymptote is $x=-1.$ This means that $k=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{ 1.5}$ and $b = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{ -1},$ and we can re-write our function as

\[ y = \dfrac{a}{x-(-1)}+1.5 = \dfrac{a}{x+1}+1.5. \]

Also, we are given that the point $(1,3.5)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

\begin{align*} y &= \dfrac{a}{x+1}+1.5 \\[5pt] 3.5 &= \dfrac{a}{1+1}+1.5 \\[5pt] 2 &= \dfrac{a}{2} \\[5pt] a &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{ 4}. \end{align*}

question.text: The diagram above shows the graph of $y = \dfrac{a}{x}.$ What is the value of $a?$
question.explanation:
Notice that the point $(3,-1)$ lies on the graph.

Substituting its coordinates into the equation $y = \dfrac{a}{x},$ we obtain

\begin{align*} -1 = \dfrac{a}{3} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad a = -3. \end{align*}
